The agent *still* did not investigate the directory; it began creating tasks again (msg 72). The user interrupted a third time (msgs 73–74): **"Sorry, it seems like you've gone into the wrong directory here. Can you understand why? Look at where the app is actually running."** Only then did the agent inspect the filesystem (msgs 77–103) and finally discover, by grepping a Claude project transcript (`.jsonl`) on disk, that the plan's files lived in a *different project directory*: `/user_c042661f/Documents/corner-play-dance/` (msg 104). The agent `cd`'d into corner-play-dance (msg 108), deleted its stale reigh tasks (msgs 114–120), read the real components (msgs 122–141), and implemented the plan: created `AnimationLifecycleContext`, `ScrollContext`, `MousePositionContext`, `FlowContext` (msgs 149–165), rewrote `App.tsx` to wrap the app in the providers (msg 172), and updated `MagicCursor`, `ColorFlowEffect`, `GlowingLetter`, `Index.tsx`, `Partner.tsx`, `FoldingHeader` (msgs 178–204). The user responded: **"That didn't fix it and you removed decorative elements that were there intentionally - also messed up the structure"** (msgs 343/345).

- **API error** at msg 273: `500 … Internal server error` mid-edit; recovered.
- **Disk full** at msgs 683–686: `df -h` showed only 245MB free; the agent cleared `~/Library/Caches/Homebrew/*` to allow a git push to proceed.

- Verification was done mostly by reading the Vite dev-server HMR log file rather than building each time; `npm run build` was run at several checkpoints and reported passing.

## Final outcome

The last user message (930) was "there are still some issues, can you see where they could be coming from?" The agent rewrote the flip cards to remove Framer Motion entirely in favor of pure CSS hover + a mobile `.is-flipped` class, confirmed compilation, and pushed `a9d0842` (msg 971). ## Problem Summary

Both the **Homepage** and **Partner page** have the same structural performance issues. The problems are duplicated across pages because shared components are wired up independently on each page.

| Issue | Impact | Homepage | Partner Page |

| `GlowingLetter` intervals | 30ms intervals per character | "ADOS" + "Save The Date" + pillar titles | Multiple headers |
| `ColorFlowEffect` | Global callback pattern | Yes | Yes |
| Off-screen animations | Wasted CPU/GPU | Scroll arrow, pillar animations | GlowingIcon infinite loops |

**Key insight:** Both pages use the same shared components (`MagicCursor`, `ColorFlowEffect`, `GlowingLetter`, `MorphingVideo`) but wire them up independently with duplicated local state.

## Solution: App-Level Context Providers

All contexts live in `App.tsx` wrapping the router, so **every page automatically benefits**:

```
App.tsx
├── ScrollProvider              ← Single scroll listener for entire app
├── MousePositionProvider       ← Single mouse listener for entire app
├── AnimationLifecycleProvider  ← Visibility tracking for entire app
├── FlowProvider                ← Particle system for entire app
└── BrowserRouter
    ├── Index (homepage)        ← Uses contexts via hooks
    └── Partner                 ← Uses contexts via hooks
```

This means:
- Add a context once → both pages improved
- Shared components become simpler (just consume context)
- No duplication of wiring code between pag
